Construction sector fragility: Bathla collapse as systemic warning

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA fourth rate hike and housing credit contraction
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce exposure to rate-sensitive REITs and construction; favour fixed-income and dividend-paying financials with strong capital buffers
Avoid leveraged construction and property developers; monitor CGP.AX, WTC.AX credit exposure; favour large-cap diversified builders
Hedge with energy equities (WDS.AX, GWO.AX) and gold; monitor oil price volatility for inflation pass-through

risk_assessment.risk_factor: ASIC regulatory action on Big Four audit firms
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor audit quality disclosures; potential reputational spillover to listed companies relying on affected firms

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Australian economic stagnation vs global peers
risk_assessment.mitigation: Diversify into international exposure; monitor GDP, retail sales, and employment data for RBA policy pivot signals

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Victoria sovereign debt and infrastructure shortfall
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor Victorian government bond spreads; assess impact on state-linked REITs and infrastructure funds

defensive_moves.rationale: Ponzi-economy dynamics in construction; Victoria debt concerns; ratings agency downgrades risk

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely range-bound with volatility. Banks provide support but housing credit contraction and fourth RBA hike create headwinds. Oil/gas and gold offer tactical upside on geopolitics. Small-caps active but speculative. Expect 2-3% index volatility over next 4-6 weeks.
market_outlook.long_term: Structural concerns around housing correction, economic stagnation, and construction sector fragility weigh on 6-12 month outlook. Energy transition and EV adoption offer secular tailwinds. RBA policy pivot likely by Q1 2027 if growth stalls. Iron ore demand softness caps mining upside. Healthcare and consumer staples remain defensive anchors.
